title: Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

reading.body:
An AI agent was deployed as an attack tool to conduct post-exploitation activity after an attacker gained initial access through a known vulnerability in marimo software. The agent operated autonomously to extract cloud credentials, retrieve an SSH private key from a cloud service, and access an internal database, completing the entire chain in under one hour. The system was not constrained to safe operations or monitored during execution.

The failure occurred in the deployment of the target systems, not the AI itself. The marimo software ran with insufficient access controls, the cloud service exposed credentials without additional authentication factors, and the internal database was accessible from a compromised SSH server with no apparent runtime detection. What would have caught this: prompt patching of the known vulnerability, credential rotation policies, network segmentation between systems of different trust levels, and active monitoring of unusual database queries and lateral movement.

It is not established whether the attacker had prior knowledge of the network architecture or whether the agent operated entirely without reconnaissance. The reports describe forensic signatures of AI orchestration rather than proof of a specific attack technique.

reports.title: AI agent at the wheel: How an attacker used LLMs to move from a CVE to an internal database in 4 pivots
AI Agent Conducted a Cyberattack on Its Own — It Took Less Than One Hour
Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

summary:
On May 10, 2026, the Sysdig Threat Research Team detected an intrusion where an artificial intelligence agent guided a cyberattack in real time. The attacker exploited a vulnerability in marimo software to gain initial access, then extracted cloud credentials and used them to retrieve an SSH private key from AWS. The attacker then accessed an internal database through an SSH server. The entire attack chain, from initial compromise to database theft, completed in under one hour. The attacker used Cloudflare Workers to distribute API calls across multiple IP addresses, making detection more difficult.

The research team identified four distinct signatures proving an AI agent orchestrated the attack rather than a pre-written script. The attacker improvised database queries against an unknown target, left planning comments in the command stream, formatted all commands for machine consumption rather than human interaction, and reused output from previous commands in subsequent operations. The team recommends immediately updating marimo to version 0.23.0, auditing credentials on exposed systems, rotating AWS credentials and database passwords, and deploying runtime threat detection across entire networks.
